title: Add built-in vise: "Fit to the stock" fails with "invalid parameters: setup 'Setup1' has no stock" and the dialog never says the stock must be set first

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat (2026-11-12, v0.18.0, with a screenshot), filed by an agent for him: "it is unclear how the built-in vise are supposed to work, and we cannot figure it out, we just get an error on fit to the stock".

**What he did.** New document, one setup (`Setup1`, active), a model imported (`Milling-test`), no stock defined yet (the browser still shows a `Stock` node under the setup). Fixtures -> Add built-in vise... -> picked "125 mm self-centering" -> left "Fit to the stock (centred, jaws closed on it)" ticked (the default) -> Place.

**What happens.** Nothing is placed. The dialog, the Fixtures page and the status bar all show, in red: `vise not placed: invalid parameters: setup 'Setup1' has no stock to fit the vise to`.

**Why.** `InsertVise::new` (`crates/app/src/commands/builtin_vise.rs`) with `VisePlacement::FitStock` reads `model::stock_world_aabb_for`, which is `None` while the setup's stock entity has no body. The refusal is right - there is nothing to fit to - but:
1. The dialog offers "Fit to the stock" ticked by default when the setup has no stock, and only says so after Place.
2. The message does not say what to do: set the stock first (Stock page), or untick the box and place the vise by position.
3. "invalid parameters:" is our word, not the user's; nothing he typed was invalid.
4. The dialog does not say how a built-in vise works at all: where it lands when fitted (fixed jaw against the stock's +Y side, centred in X, jaw floor under the stock, opening = the stock's Y width; a self-centering one centred in X and Y), what the figures mean for the fit, and that the placed vise is then judged in the collision checks.
5. The browser shows a `Stock` node for a setup whose stock has no body, so "has no stock" reads as wrong.

**Wanted**
- When the active setup has no stock body: the dialog says so before Place, in plain English ("This setup has no stock yet. Set the stock (Stock page) to fit the vise to it, or place the vise by position below."), with a button that opens the Stock page; "Fit to the stock" is off and greyed with that reason, and the position rows show.
- With a stock: one or two plain lines under the checkbox saying where the vise will land and how far the jaws open, from the stock's real figures (e.g. "Opens to 80.0 mm on the stock's Y width; stock sits on the jaw floor"), and a named refusal up front when the stock is wider than the vise's max opening.
- Refusal texts on this path lose the "invalid parameters:" prefix and say what to do next.
- The same for the two siblings that fail the same way: "Add mod vise pair" (`commands/mod_vise.rs`, "has no stock to fit the mod vise to") and parallels under the stock (`commands/accessory.rs`, "has no stock to fit the parallels under").
- A stock that has no body yet is shown as such in the browser (e.g. `Stock  not set`), the way `Machine  no machine` is.

Not wanted here: fitting the vise to the part instead of the stock, or creating a stock automatically - a vise holds the stock; if a default stock at import is wanted, that is its own issue.

Done means: on a setup without stock the dialog explains and offers the Stock page before any Place, and Place by position works; with a stock, Fit places the vise and the dialog said beforehand where; the three refusals read in plain English; pinned in the structural tests (labels, the greyed checkbox and its reason, the button) and by app tests for the refusal texts. No command semantics change; no snapshot PNG touched.
